questions.title: Recursive GCD
questions.description:
Compute the greatest common divisor of two positive integers with the recursive Euclidean algorithm: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b), stopping when the second number is 0. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long gcd_rec(long long a, long long b)

Input Format:
One line with a and b.

Output Format:
One line with gcd(a, b).

Constraints:
1 <= a, b <= 1000000

questions.title: Binary Digits by Recursion
questions.description:
A hardware course displays numbers in base 2. Build the binary representation recursively: the bits of n are the bits of n / 2 followed by the last bit of n. Report the value without leading zeros (n >= 1, so the output always starts with 1). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string to_binary(long long n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the binary representation of n (no leading zeros).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi Move Plan
questions.description:
Print the full minimal move plan for the Tower of Hanoi: move n disks from peg A to peg C using peg B as the spare, one disk per move, never on a smaller disk. Solve recursively: to move k disks from X to Y via Z, first move k-1 disks X to Z via Y, then move disk k printing "disk k: X->Y", then move k-1 disks Z to Y via X. Loops are banned — pure recursion; append each move line to the returned vector with push_back. The harness prints the moves space-separated on one line. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<std::string> hanoi_plan(int n)

Input Format:
One line with the number of disks.

Output Format:
One line with the moves in order, e.g. for 2 disks: disk 1: A->B disk 2: A->C disk 1: B->C

Constraints:
1 <= disks <= 4
questions.sampleoutput1: disk 1: A->B disk 2: A->C disk 1: B->C
questions.output1: disk 1: A->C disk 2: A->B disk 1: C->B disk 3: A->C disk 1: B->A disk 2: B->C disk 1: A->C
questions.output2: disk 1: A->B disk 2: A->C disk 1: B->C disk 3: A->B disk 1: C->A disk 2: C->B disk 1: A->B disk 4: A->C disk 1: B->C disk 2: B->A disk 1: C->A disk 3: B->C disk 1: A->B disk 2: A->C disk 1: B->C
questions.output3: disk 1: A->B disk 2: A->C disk 1: B->C

questions.title: Recursive Factorial
questions.description:
Compute n! recursively — the product of all integers from 1 to n, with 0! = 1 by definition. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long factorial(int n)

It must return n! computed with recursion (a base case plus a recursive call).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with n!.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 20

questions.title: Recursive Fibonacci
questions.description:
Compute the n-th Fibonacci number recursively: fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1, and fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2) for n >= 2. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fibonacci(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with fib(n).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 25

questions.title: Recursive Digit Sum
questions.description:
Sum the decimal digits of a non-negative number recursively: strip the last digit, recurse on what remains, and stop at a single digit. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int digit_sum(long long n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the sum of the digits of n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000000

questions.title: Recursive String Reversal
questions.description:
Reverse a word recursively: the reverse of a word is the reverse of its tail followed by its first character. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string reverse_string(const std::string &s)

It must return the reversed word (the original must not be modified).

Input Format:
One line with a single word (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line with the reversed word.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 500, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Recursive Vector Total
questions.description:
Add up a vector of integers recursively: the total of an empty suffix is 0, and the total at index i is v[i] plus the total of the rest. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long vector_sum(const std::vector<int> &v)

It must return the sum of all elements, computed with recursion (no loops).

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the total.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -1000000 <= values <= 1000000

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Route Count
questions.description:
A porter must climb a staircase of n steps and can take either 1 or 2 steps at a time. Count the distinct routes recursively: with 0 steps left there is exactly 1 route (stop), and from any landing the porter branches into the 1-step and the 2-step move. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long climb_ways(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct routes.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 30

questions.title: Palindrome Name Check by Recursion
questions.description:
A signup form only accepts palindrome usernames. Check recursively with two indices: the outer characters must match and the inner substring must be a palindrome. Report 1 for a palindrome and 0 otherwise. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_palindrome(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single word (no spaces).

Output Format:
One line: 1 if the word reads the same forwards and backwards, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= word length <= 500, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Collatz Countdown Recursively
questions.description:
The Collatz process repeats: if n is even, replace it with n / 2; if n is odd, replace it with 3n + 1; the process stops at 1. Count how many replacements (steps) are needed to reach 1, computed recursively — collatz_steps(1) = 0. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long collatz_steps(long long n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of steps to reach 1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000

questions.title: Fast Power by Repeated Squaring
questions.description:
A geometry utility needs base raised to a non-negative exponent quickly. Use recursive repeated squaring: x^e = (x^(e/2))^2, multiplied by x once more when e is odd. Loops are banned — solve it purely with recursion. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fast_pow(long long base, long long exp)

Input Format:
One line with base and exp.

Output Format:
One line with base^exp.

Constraints:
|base| <= 1000, 0 <= exp <= 60, the true result always fits in a signed 64-bit integer
questions.inputconstrains: |base| <= 1000, 0 <= exp <= 60, the true result always fits in a signed 64-bit integer

questions.title: Tower of Hanoi Move Count
questions.description:
The classic puzzle: move a tower of n disks from one peg to another using one spare peg, never placing a bigger disk on a smaller one. The minimum number of moves satisfies moves(1) = 1 and moves(n) = 2 * moves(n-1) + 1. Compute it recursively — loops are banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long hanoi_moves(int disks)

Input Format:
One line with the number of disks.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of moves.

Constraints:
1 <= disks <= 30

questions.title: Count Subsets with Exact Sum
questions.description:
A gift shop packs bundles: every item may be included or left out, and a bundle is valid when its items sum exactly to S. Count the valid bundles with an include/exclude recursion over the item positions. Two bundles are different if they use a different set of positions, so equal values may be counted multiple times. Calling a sort routine is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long count_subsets(const std::vector<int> &v, int S)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: S.

Output Format:
One line with the number of position-subsets summing exactly to S.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 15, 1 <= values <= 100, 1 <= S <= 300

questions.title: Count Distinct Word Arrangements
questions.description:
A word-game server counts how many DISTINCT arrangements (permutations) a rack of letters has — arrangements that differ only by swapping identical letters count once. Count them with a backtracking recursion over letter frequencies: at each position try every letter type that still has copies left. std::next_permutation is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long count_arrangements(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
Line 1: n (the word length). Line 2: the word of n lowercase letters.

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct arrangements.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 8, lowercase letters only

questions.title: Dice Sequences Hitting the Target
questions.description:
A board-game app replays luck: how many ordered sequences of die rolls (each roll 1-6) sum exactly to the target square? Recurse on the remaining target — after rolling face f, the rest of the sequence must sum to target - f — and loop over the six faces at each step. Memo tables (maps / hash containers) are banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long count_rolls(int target)

Input Format:
One line with target.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ordered roll sequences summing exactly to target.

Constraints:
1 <= target <= 22

questions.title: Robot Paths Around Puddles
questions.description:
A warehouse robot walks from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell of a grid, moving only RIGHT or DOWN. Cells marked 1 are puddles and may not be entered. Count the valid routes with a recursive walk: from each free cell branch into the two moves; stepping outside the grid or into a puddle contributes nothing. Memo tables (maps / hash containers) are banned — let the recursion tree do the work. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long count_paths(const std::vector<std::vector<int>> &grid)

Input Format:
Line 1: r and c. Lines 2..r+1: r lines with c cells each (0 = free, 1 = puddle).

Output Format:
One line with the number of valid routes.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 8, cells are 0 or 1, the start and end cells are free
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= r, c <= 8, cells are 0 or 1, the start and end cells are free

questions.title: K-th Lexicographic Permutation
questions.description:
A lockscreen puzzle generates passcodes from letters. You receive n DISTINCT letters already in ascending alphabetical order and a 1-based rank k; return the k-th permutation of the letters in lexicographic order (the 1st is the sorted order itself). Build the answer iteratively: pick which letter leads the next position by dividing the remaining rank by the block size (n-1)!, then shrink. std::next_permutation is banned. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string kth_permutation(int n, const std::string &letters, long long k)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: the n distinct letters in ascending order. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th lexicographic permutation.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 8, letters are distinct and given ascending, 1 <= k <= n!
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 8, letters are distinct and given ascending, 1 <= k <= n!

questions.title: List All Subsets Summing to S
questions.description:
A promo builder lists every bundle whose items sum exactly to S. The values are given already ASCENDING and DISTINCT, so sorting is unnecessary — calling a sort routine is banned. Enumerate with a "start index" recursion: for each start position, take that value, record the subset when the sum is reached, then extend it only with values that come later. This produces each subset with ascending elements and lists the subsets in lexicographic (dictionary) order of their element sequences, where a prefix sorts before its extensions. Example: values 1 2 3 4, S = 5 yields two lines: "1 4" then "2 3". The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::vector<std::vector<int>> subset_sums(const std::vector<int> &v, int S)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n ascending distinct integers. Line 3: S.

Output Format:
One line per subset, elements space-separated, in the order described above.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 12, 1 <= values <= 100 ascending and distinct, 1 <= S <= 300, at least one subset exists
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 12, 1 <= values <= 100 ascending and distinct, 1 <= S <= 300, at least one subset exists

questions.title: N-Queens Solution Count
questions.description:
A chess trainer counts the solutions of the n-queens puzzle: place n queens on an n x n board so that no two share a row, column or diagonal. Place queens row by row with recursive backtracking: for the current row try every column, keep it only if no earlier queen attacks it, recurse, then undo. Return the total number of distinct solutions. std::next_permutation is banned — enumerate the placements yourself. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long nqueens_count(int n)

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of solutions.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 6
